newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end higher on tax relief expectations.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end higher on tax relief expectations.

text.p: Shares on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed higher as financial institutions made purchases amid expectations the government will announce an exemption from a proposed minimum tax for selected industries, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 4.66 points higher at 807.59.
"Encouraging first quarter performance by some companies aided the market," said Shree Bhagwan of brokers Means Leasing.
Brokers said they expected Finance Minister P. Chidambaram to announce some concessions in tax proposals made in the 1996/97 (April-March) budget when he addresses parliament this week.
Officials said he was expected to speak on Tuesday after parliament adjourned on Monday without transacting any business following the death of a sitting member.
Chidambaram was scheduled to present on Monday a reply to a preliminary debate on the general aspects of the budget.
TISCO firmed 5.35 rupees to 201.60 on institutional support, brokers said.
State Bank of India quoted 9.20 rupees up at 283.95 on speculative buying while ITC ended 7.30 rupees higher at 298.80, they said.
ACC rose 35 rupees to 2,220. Reliance Industries rose 3.05 rupees to 215.40.
